titulo: Bond Yields Surge and Oil Shocks Shake Markets
resumo: October 2026 brought intense turbulence to global financial markets as **soaring bond yields** hit multi-year highs and renewed geopolitical conflict pushed Brent crude near $100. Central bank minutes revealed a **hawkish unity** over ongoing inflation pressures, prompting mortgage rates to climb significantly. Meanwhile, AI sentiment cooled amid valuation and revenue questions, though major indexes found occasional support from dip-buyers.

themes.texto: Government debt markets experienced severe downward pressure, driving benchmark yields to levels not seen in decades. The sell-off reflected persistent worries about government borrowing and stubborn inflation readings.

Crude prices spiked toward $100 following supply restrictions and Middle East tensions, prompting G7 discussions over emergency fuel reserves. The energy surge added fresh cost pressures for consumers and businesses alike.

themes.titulo: AI Sentiment and Tech Reality Check
themes.texto: High-flying artificial intelligence stocks faced a reality check after revenue reports and canceled public offerings stirred bubble fears. Investors began scrutinizing the actual monetary payoffs behind heavy infrastructure spending.

Economic data revealed a sharp slowdown in hiring as the US added just 29,000 jobs in September and unemployment ticked up to 4.2%. The weaker labor figures altered market expectations regarding near-term central bank actions.

momentos.facto: Treasury 10-year yields hit their highest level since 2002 while UK long-term bond yields reached 6% for the first time since 1998.
US jobs data showed growth slowed sharply to 29,000 in September as the unemployment rate rose to 4.2%.
The euro slid to a 17-month low against the dollar amid growing fiscal turmoil and debt fears in France.
The S&P 500 climbed to a record high as tech and AI bulls drove a brief market recovery.
Federal Reserve minutes from the September meeting revealed hawkish unity behind maintaining a tight stance against inflation.
US mortgage rates climbed for the seventh straight week, reaching their highest levels since 2023.
